findings.severity: high if replacements are not disabled
findings.exploit_path: Repository-local refs/replace maps changed candidate commit to trusted commit; normal Git object reads then bind replacement contents rather than supplied object contents.
findings.evidence: After git -C FIXTURE replace CHANGED TRUSTED, git -C FIXTURE ls-tree -z CHANGED -- tools/runner.py exited 0 and returned blob 51fff255b05322704120ab22c35b8a96b8985bca. With git --no-replace-objects -C FIXTURE ls-tree -z CHANGED -- tools/runner.py, exit 0 returned real changed blob 6541d6efa8ac1cf6ccca653e0fe2c0a6c562f5ba.
findings.impact: False equality is possible in implementations that only sanitize inherited GIT_* variables. Local replacements survive that sanitization.
findings.smallest_remediation: Apply --no-replace-objects to every Git invocation, or explicitly set GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1 after environment sanitization.

findings.exploit_path: A branch and tag share an unqualified trusted revision name but point to different commits.
findings.evidence: git -C FIXTURE rev-parse --verify --end-of-options ambiguous^{commit} exited 0, returned trusted tag OID 9767e896d19964113a467c69dbfe4822c436ad5a, and warned refname 'ambiguous' is ambiguous; branch pointed to changed OID.
findings.impact: A verifier expecting the branch can unintentionally supply the tag's source. This is not an author-independent trust violation when the verifier intentionally supplies the resolved object.
findings.smallest_remediation: Verifier supplies a full trusted commit object ID. Resolve revisions once to full IDs before further object reads; do not interpret successful rev-parse as ambiguity rejection.

findings.exploit_path: Inherited GIT_DIR redirects repository selection despite explicit -C.
findings.evidence: GIT_DIR=/fast/scratch/hyaku/tameshi-r59/T59W1S57/nonexistent git -C FIXTURE rev-parse --show-toplevel exited 128: fatal: not a git repository: '/fast/scratch/hyaku/tameshi-r59/T59W1S57/nonexistent'.
findings.impact: Untrusted ambient Git variables can redirect or disable reads; environment-based config can also alter Git semantics.
findings.smallest_remediation: Remove all inherited GIT_* variables and set intentional controls explicitly, including global/system config isolation and replacement suppression.
